labels.text: section 6651(a)/(i): the dollar amount for the 60-day-late minimum failure-to-file addition. NOTE: the statute's own trigger is the RETURN'S due date ("returns the due date for which ... is after December 31, 20xx"), a different time axis than this dataset's legal_time; the boundaries below approximate that trigger by the following calendar year, a documented simplification (see report).
$100, as enacted by Pub. L. 97-248 §318(a) (1982), applicable to returns the due date for filing of which (including extensions) is after Dec. 31, 1982
$135, substituted by Pub. L. 110-245 §303(a), applicable to returns required to be filed after Dec. 31, 2008

$205, substituted by Pub. L. 114-125 §921(a), applicable to returns required to be filed in calendar years after 2015. The intervening $330 figure (Pub. L. 116-25 §3201(a), enacted July 1, 2019, nominally 'applicable to returns required to be filed after December 31, 2019') was itself superseded by the $435 figure below (Pub. L. 116-94 §402(a), enacted Dec. 20, 2019, same applicability trigger) before any return became subject to it, and so is omitted as never operative — noted, not silently dropped.

$435, substituted by Pub. L. 116-94 §402(a), applicable to returns the due date for which (including extensions) is after Dec. 31, 2019; the pinned USCODE-2024-title26 edition text of subsection (a) itself states this figure. SOURCE_GAP: subsection (j) directs a further annual cost-of-living increase for returns required to be filed in calendar years after 2020 (published by Revenue Procedure, not by this snapshot's pinned bytes) — those figures are NOT entered here; see coverage row 26/6651/j/u1 and report.
